I am an old man here in Shinyanga, farming this land like my father did. This plot is big — almost eight hectares — and I plant it mixed with my crops together as I always do. The rains here are not so much, sometimes the season is dry and the harvest is small, so I do not waste my shillings on fertilizer from the shop — none of my neighbors here use it on land like this, and I do not trust to spend money I may lose. I keep some cattle and goats, so I spread their manure on the parts near the homestead, and I use my own seeds saved from last harvest like I have always done. For this big plot, my sons and their wives help me, and at weeding time and harvest I call some young men from the village and pay them a little or feed them.
